subject: General Knowledge
description: Covers Losar, Hornbill, Chhath, Ambubachi, Shirui Lily, Jallikattu, and New Year festivals.

questions.stem: Losar is a prominent festival celebrating the New Year in which Indian region/state?

options.option_text: Ladakh and Sikkim
Kerala
Assam
Gujarat

questions.explanation:
LOSAR FESTIVAL: The Tibetan New Year, widely celebrated in the Himalayan regions of India with significant Buddhist populations, primarily Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, and the Lahaul-Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh. It involves elaborate prayers, chanting, traditional mask dances (Cham dance), and feasting. 
- Kerala celebrates Vishu (Malayalam New Year).
- Assam celebrates Rongali Bihu (Assamese New Year).
- Gujarat celebrates Bestu Varas (Gujarati New Year). PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, RRB, State PSCs.

questions.stem: The Hornbill Festival, often called the "Festival of Festivals", is held annually in the first week of December in which state?

options.option_text: Nagaland
Manipur
Mizoram
Meghalaya

questions.explanation: HORNBILL FESTIVAL: A massive, 10-day cultural extravaganza held every year from Dec 1 to 10 in Nagaland at the Kisama Heritage Village. Organized by the State Tourism and Art & Culture Departments, it showcases the rich culture, traditional dances, sports, and crafts of all the Naga tribes. It is named after the Indian Hornbill, a bird revered in Naga folklore. PYQ FREQUENCY: Highly repeated across UPSC Prelims, SSC, and Banking exams.

questions.stem: Which of the following festivals is dedicated to the worship of the Sun God and his wife Usha, and is primarily celebrated in Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh?

options.option_text: Chhath Puja
Makar Sankranti
Bihu
Ugadi

questions.explanation: CHHATH PUJA: An ancient Hindu Vedic festival historically native to the Indian subcontinent, more specifically, the states of Bihar, Jharkhand, and eastern Uttar Pradesh (Purvanchal), as well as the Madhesh region of Nepal. The Puja is dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya (Usha, the dawn) to thank them for bestowing the bounties of life on earth. Uniquely, it involves offering prayers to the setting sun as well as the rising sun. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CHSL, CGL, State PSCs.

questions.stem: The famous "Ambubachi Mela" is an annual Hindu mela held at which renowned temple?

options.option_text: Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati (Assam)
Jagannath Temple, Puri (Odisha)
Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Varanasi (UP)
Meenakshi Temple, Madurai (Tamil Nadu)

questions.explanation: AMBUBACHI MELA: An annual festival held at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam during the monsoon season (June). It celebrates the annual menstruation course of the presiding goddess, Maa Kamakhya. The temple remains closed for three days, and on the fourth day, devotees throng the temple for blessings. It is one of the most important congregations of Tantric ascetics. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims (Culture), SSC CGL, APSC.

questions.stem: Which state celebrates the "Shirui Lily Festival" to spread awareness about its state flower?

options.option_text: Manipur
Sikkim
Uttarakhand
Himachal Pradesh

questions.explanation:
SHIRUI LILY FESTIVAL: Celebrated in Manipur (specifically in the Ukhrul district) to promote and protect the Shirui Lily (Lilium mackliniae), which is the State Flower of Manipur. This rare bell-shaped flower grows only in the Shirui Hill ranges and nowhere else in the world. 
- Sikkim celebrates the International Flower Festival (Orchids).
- Uttarakhand is famous for the Valley of Flowers. PYQ FREQUENCY: Current Affairs, SSC, State PSCs.

questions.stem: The harvest festival of "Pongal" in Tamil Nadu spans four days. What is the traditional bull-taming sport associated with the third day (Mattu Pongal)?

options.option_text: Jallikattu
Kambala
Vallam Kali
Mallakhamb

questions.explanation:
PONGAL AND JALLIKATTU: Pongal is a four-day harvest festival in Tamil Nadu (Bhogi, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal, Kaanum Pongal). Mattu Pongal (the 3rd day) is dedicated to cattle. JALLIKATTU is a traditional spectacle/sport where a bull is released into a crowd of people, and participants attempt to grab the large hump on the bull's back. 
- KAMBALA: Buffalo race in muddy fields in Karnataka.
- VALLAM KALI: Snake boat race in Kerala.
- MALLAKHAMB: Traditional pole gymnastics from Maharashtra/MP. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL.

questions.stem: In the context of regional New Year festivals in India, which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.option_text: Gudi Padwa - Gujarat
Puthandu - Tamil Nadu
Navreh - Kashmir
Ugadi - Andhra Pradesh/Telangana/Karnataka

questions.explanation:
INDIAN NEW YEARS: 
- GUDI PADWA is the traditional New Year for Marathi and Konkani Hindus in MAHARASHTRA, Goa, and Daman. 
- Bestu Varas is the Gujarati New Year (celebrated a day after Diwali).
- PUTHANDU: Tamil New Year (mid-April).
- NAVREH: Kashmiri Pandit New Year.
- UGADI: Telugu and Kannada New Year (Chaitra Sukladi). 
- POILA BOISHAKH: Bengali New Year.
- BOHAG BIHU (Rongali Bihu): Assamese New Year. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims GS-1 (Culture), SSC.

questions.stem: The elaborate floral carpet laid on the ground as a central ritual during Onam celebrations in Kerala is known as?

options.option_text: Pookalam — concentric rings of flowers arranged on the floor
Kolam — geometric rice-flour patterns drawn at home entrances
Alpana — white rice-paste floor art traditional in West Bengal
Muggu — colourful floor design practised in Andhra Pradesh homes

questions.explanation: Pookalam is the tiered floral carpet created over ten days of Onam using fresh flowers, growing more elaborate each day until Thiruvonam. Kolam/Muggu/Alpana are analogous floor arts from other states but are NOT the Onam-specific term; confusing them with Pookalam is a common distractor error.

questions.stem: The Pushkar Fair, one of India's largest camel and livestock fairs held during Kartik Purnima, is located in which state?

options.option_text: Gujarat — home to the Rann of Kutch Utsav and White Rann festival
Haryana — known for the Surajkund International Crafts Mela nearby
Rajasthan — held at Pushkar near Ajmer during Kartik Purnima
Madhya Pradesh — hosts the famous Khajuraho Dance Festival annually

questions.explanation: Pushkar is a town in Ajmer district, Rajasthan; the fair coincides with Kartik Purnima (Oct–Nov). Gujarat's Rann Utsav is a common distractor since both involve desert/arid landscapes and large cultural fairs, but they are entirely different events in different states.

questions.stem: The 'Wangala' festival, popularly called the Hundred Drums Festival, is the post-harvest celebration of which tribal community?

options.option_text: Khasi community of the Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya
Garo community of Meghalaya, honouring the Sun deity Saljong
Bodo community of Assam, celebrated after the rice transplanting
Naga community observed across multiple hill districts of Nagaland

questions.explanation: Wangala is exclusively a Garo tribal festival of Meghalaya celebrated after the paddy harvest in November; it honours Saljong, their Sun deity, with traditional drumming and dances. Khasi and Bodo are plausible distractors because they are also major NE tribal groups in the same region, but neither community owns the Wangala tradition.

questions.stem: Thrissur Pooram, considered the 'mother of all Poorams' in Kerala, is centred around which temple as the presiding venue?

options.option_text: Lord Vishnu — worshipped in the Ranganatha form at Thrissur's shrine
Goddess Bhagavathy — the presiding deity of both competing Pooram groups
Lord Shiva — enshrined at Vadakkumnathan, the Pooram's central venue
Lord Murugan — the war deity honoured in this annual Trichur celebration

questions.explanation: The Vadakkumnathan Temple at the heart of Thrissur is a Shiva temple; the Pooram spectacle is held in its grounds. Option B is the most tempting distractor because the two competing groups — Thiruvambady and Paramekkavu — are both Bhagavathy temples, but the host/central venue deity is Lord Shiva, not Bhagavathy.

questions.stem: The 'Bali Yatra' festival celebrated on the banks of the Mahanadi in Cuttack, Odisha, commemorates which historical tradition?

options.option_text: Annual tribute voyages sent by Odishan kings to the Mughal emperor
Ancient Odishan Sadhabas sailing to Bali and Southeast Asian islands
Sea-bath rituals of Lord Jagannath's idol at Puri's Chilika lake shores
Historic naval expeditions by the Gajapati dynasty in the Bay of Bengal

questions.explanation: Bali Yatra (literally 'voyage to Bali') marks the departure of ancient Odishan sea-merchants called Sadhabas who sailed on Kartik Purnima to Bali, Java, Sumatra, and Sri Lanka for trade. Option C is a common confusion because Jagannath and Puri are iconic Odisha associations, but the sea-bath ritual (Snanayatra) is an entirely separate event.

questions.stem: The 'Chapchar Kut' festival of Mizoram is celebrated in March as a community rejoicing that specifically marks the completion of which stage in jhum cultivation?

options.option_text: Completion of paddy transplanting into the terraced hill-slope fields
Felling and burning of jungle undergrowth to prepare jhum plots
Harvesting of the main crops and storing produce in community granaries
Digging and alignment of irrigation channels before the Kharif sowing

questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut (celebrated in March) comes after the most labour-intensive phase of jhum — felling trees and burning the cleared plot — but before actual sowing begins. This timing is precise: Option C (harvest) would place it in autumn, and Option A (transplanting) does not apply to the rain-fed jhum system which uses direct sowing, not transplanting.

questions.stem: During Kumbh Mela, 'Mauni Amavasya' is regarded as the single most auspicious Shahi Snan day. What does the term 'Mauni' specifically signify for pilgrims observing this occasion?

options.option_text: Pilgrims observing a vow of complete silence throughout the bathing day
Collective chanting of Vedic hymns (mantras) at the Triveni Sangam
Offering of moong dal (green lentils) to the holy Ganga as thanksgiving
Mass lighting of earthen diyas along all river ghats after evening prayers

questions.explanation: Mauni derives from 'mauna' (Sanskrit for silence); on Mauni Amavasya pilgrims traditionally observe a vow of complete silence from dawn to dusk while bathing at the Sangam. Option B is the most plausible distractor because Vedic chanting is prominently associated with the Kumbh bathing ritual, but 'mauni' specifically refers to the silence vow, not chanting — the two practices are actually opposites.
